subject: MSA redlines and change-order path for capacity/pricing
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@syncwave.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@syncwave.ai, Paul Miles <paul.miles@syncwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SyncWave MSA redlines (first pass)

Connor — attaching our first-pass redlines to the MSA and order form. The big items for us are: 1) a clearer SLA escalation path (we need an operational contact and 4-hour response objective for severity-1 incidents), 2) explicit data residency and deletion language for EU-subset datasets, and 3) a one-off credit if the initial throughput ramp underperforms our agreed benchmark.

We marked inline comments in the attached Word file (MSA_SyncWave_redlines_v3.docx). Paul is looped in for procurement specifics. We prefer to get to a negotiated position this week if possible — can you confirm who on Redwood legal will take point?

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Partnerships
SyncWave

Attachment: MSA_SyncWave_redlines_v3.docx (docx, 124 KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@syncwave.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SyncWave MSA redlines (first pass)

Emily — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the detailed inline notes. I reviewed the doc and forwarded to our legal and finance leads (cc'd). Proposed plan:

- Internal sync with legal + finance today to triage redlines and categorize into (i) accept as-is, (ii) minor wording tweaks, (iii) terms that require business sign-off (pricing/credits) or product mitigation (data residency).
- Karthik suggested we separate platform-level MSA redlines from order-form change orders (capacity/pricing). My preference is to accept the MSA with tracked exceptions where possible and handle the capacity/credit items via a Change Order so we can keep implementation moving.
- I'll own the Canvass/approval playbook and will circulate a change_order_framework.xlsx that outlines commitment windows, staged ramp, and acceptance criteria.

Can you confirm SyncWave's priority on the SLA vs the credit? If SLA is highest priority we'll prioritize that first in our redline response. Proposed next milestone: short internal legal notes by EOD tomorrow, then a joint 30-min call Wednesday to agree on the three items.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Direct: (415) 555-0128
connor.obrien@redwood.com

Attachment: change_order_framework.xlsx (xlsx, 22 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SyncWave MSA redlines (first pass)

Folks — quick legal triage after reviewing Emily's redlines and Connor's note. High-level takeaways:

1) SLA / Escalation: we can accept a 4-hour acknowledgement commitment for Sev-1 and we can map an operational contact; however, the remediation SLA language as written is open-ended. Suggest we counter with: "Acknowledgement within 4 hours; action plan within 24 hours; target remediation time to be mutually agreed per incident severity and documented in the runbook." That keeps us workable for multi-region incidents.

2) Data residency & deletion: redline requires specific EU residency guarantee. Product/infra note: we can offer a contractual commitment to store EU-designated datasets in the EU region for an initial 12-month term with an associated implementation fee for guarded provisioning. We should flag this as a scope & cost item to be captured in a Change Order (CO-02).

3) Throughput/credit ask: the credit request tied to benchmark underperformance is commercial in nature. Recommend capturing this as a capped credit (e.g., up to 10% of month-1 invoice) and pairing it with acceptance criteria and a remediation plan. Finance (Laura) — please advise on cap tolerances.

4) Indemnity & limitation tweaks: there are aggressive indemnity asks in the redline. We should propose language parity and not expand Redwood's exposure. Suggest we provide a marked counter in the attached legal_notes_syncwave_20260519.pdf.

Next steps: Connor — propose we accept the MSA with tracked exceptions on indemnity/data residency and create Change Order #2 to cover EU residency provisioning + throughput ramp credits + SLA runbook commitments. I can draft the legal redline to circulate for SyncWave review; if agreed, we aim to get signatures on CO-02 and the MSA amendment in one DocuSign packet.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
Attachment: legal_notes_syncwave_20260519.pdf (pdf, 48 KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@syncwave.ai>, Paul Miles <paul.miles@syncwave.ai>, legal@syncwave.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SyncWave MSA redlines (first pass) — proposed path forward

Emily / Paul — looping you back with our proposed path so we can get an execution timeline locked in. Summary and asks:  

- MSA: Redwood proposes to accept the MSA with three tracked exceptions (indemnity parity language, clarified incident remediation timing, and data residency scope). Karthik will send a marked counter later today.
- Change Order (CO-02): we will capture EU data residency provisioning (12-month term, implementation fee), the throughput acceptance benchmark and a capped remedial credit (proposal: up to 10% of month-1 invoice if benchmarks missed), and a staged ramp plan (2-week canary at 50% capacity followed by full ramp). The attached change_order_framework.xlsx contains the ramp windows and acceptance criteria.
- Timing & sign-off: proposed schedule — legal redline and CO-02 draft by EOD Fri (my ask), internal approvals over the weekend, DocuSign packet Monday morning. If SyncWave approves, your confirmation reply is sufficient to route for signatures; otherwise request a 30-min alignment call Monday.

Related links: DocuSign packet preview: https://docusign.com/sign/abcdef1234567890  | Shared redline drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSyncWaveRedlines

Action items for SyncWave: please confirm (i) SLA escalation priority (SLA first / credit first), and (ii) authority to sign for CO-02 (is Paul the procurement signee?). Once confirmed we will publish CO-02 and route.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | (415) 555-0128
